newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali reconciliation conference set for June 10.
newsitem.headline: Somali reconciliation conference set for June 10.

text.p: A coalition of Somali factions on Monday called a national reconciliation conference for June 10 in the northeastern Somali port of Bosasso to set up a new government.

The 26 factions of the National Salvation Council (NSC), formed in Ethiopia in January after weeks of talks, said 1,000 delegates would attend the conference to establish a government of national unity.
However, faction chief Hussein Aideed, based in south Mogadishu, has boycotted the talks and said the NSC was the result of Ethiopian interference in Somalia.
Aideed was elected by supporters as president of Somalia after the death of his father Mohamed Farah Aideed last August. The NSC factions reject both his presidency and his government.
Addressing an NSC meeting on Monday, North Mogadishu faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed said talks between his and Aideed's factions on bringing peace to the capital were making progress.
Somalia has had no central government since the fall of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991. Faction leaders then turned their guns on each other, creating a famine that killed 300,000 people.
